resolved.rationale: Reviewer A claims: Inconsistent Option Naming

Reviewer A claims: Description: The option name `OpenMetricsSkipSTSeries` is inconsistent with its actual behavior. The name suggests it skips ST series, but it actually controls whether to parse start timestamps. This could lead to confusion. Consider renaming to something like `ParseStartTimestamps` for clarity.
Reviewer A claims: Missing Test Coverage for parseST=false
Reviewer A claims: Description: The new conditional logic for `parseST` is not fully tested in the test files. There should be explicit test cases verifying behavior when `parseST` is false.

Reviewer A claims: Description: The comment explaining `OpenMetricsSkipSTSeries` is incomplete. It should clearly document that when true, start timestamp parsing will be skipped for performance reasons.
Reviewer A claims: The conditional start timestamp parsing could lead to subtle bugs if not handled carefully throughout the codebase, though current changes look correct.

Reviewer A claims: The performance optimization (skipping start timestamp parsing) might not be significant enough to justify the added complexity, though this would need benchmarking data to confirm.
Reviewer A claims: Good separation of concerns in the implementation
Reviewer A claims: Existing tests were updated to include the new option
Reviewer A claims: Clear addition of the new benchmark case
Reviewer A claims: The change is backward compatible

Reviewer B claims: The test cases in `nhcbparse_test.go` have been updated to include `OpenMetricsSkipSTSeries: true` in the `ParserOptions`. However, the comments and the context around these changes do not clearly explain why this option is being set to `true` in all cases. This could lead to confusion or inconsiste

Reviewer B claims: The new field `parseST` in the `NHCBParser` struct is not documented. This could make the code harder to understand and maintain. It is important to document new fields to explain their purpose and usage.

Reviewer B claims: In the `processClassicHistogramSeries` method, the `tempST` is set to `0` when `p.parseST` is `false`. This might lead to unexpected behavior if other parts of the code assume that `tempST` will always be a valid timestamp. It is important to ensure that this change does not break any existing funct

Reviewer B claims: The comments in the `BenchmarkParseOpenMetricsNHCB` function have inconsistent spacing. The first two comments have one space after the `//`, while the new comment has two spaces. Maintaining a consistent code style is important for readability and maintainability.

Reviewer B claims: The change to skip start timestamp parsing when `OpenMetricsSkipSTSeries` is `true` might have performance implications. While the change is intended to optimize performance, it is important to ensure that this optimization does not negatively impact other parts of the system or introduce new bugs.

Reviewer B claims: The addition of the `OpenMetricsSkipSTSeries` option and the changes to the `NHCBParser` might affect backward compatibility. It is important to ensure that existing code that relies on the previous behavior continues to work as expected.

Reviewer B claims: The changes introduce new functionality and options. It is crucial to ensure that the test coverage is adequate to catch any potential issues. The test cases should be updated to cover all new scenarios and edge cases.
Reviewer A claims: Potential Performance Impact

Reviewer A claims: Description: The new conditional start timestamp parsing could have performance implications that aren't benchmarked. The benchmark tests should include cases with `parseST=false` to measure the performance difference.
Reviewer A claims: The changes introduce a new parser variant (`omtext_with_nhcb_st`) which increases maintenance complexity.
